ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit diagram is a complementary symmetrical power amplifier circuit; the output terminal on the right is labeled uo, and the load resistor is labeled 8Ω; the power supply is vertically symmetrical, with the upper end labeled +15V and the lower end labeled -15V; the output stage is composed of two complementary transistors, VT1 and VT2. The problem statement gives that the transistor saturation voltage drop is approximately |UCES|≈3V. Reasoning: Since a ±15V split power supply is used, the maximum undistorted peak values of the positive and negative half-cycles of the output are limited by the power supply voltage and the transistor saturation voltage drop. The maximum output peak voltage is 15V - 3V = 12V. The RMS value of the sinusoidal output is Urms = 12/√2 V. The load is 8Ω, so the maximum undistorted output power POM = Urms^2 / R = (12/√2)^2 / 8 = 12^2 / (2×8) = 144/16 = 9W.
